speaker: Unknown
en: The most important skill in this industry, or perhaps in the world, is your ability to identify things before the market.
zh: 这个行业里最重要的技能,或许在全世界也是,就是你在市场之前识别出事物的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are so many people in the world who we want to meet who also want to meet us.
zh: 世界上有那么多我们想见、而他们也想见我们的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just an information problem.
zh: 而这只是一个信息问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's more impressive to you, someone who went to Stanford or someone who is followed by Patrick Collison, Elon Musk, Marc Andreessen?
zh: 对你来说哪个更令人印象深刻,一个上过斯坦福的人,还是一个被 Patrick Collison、Elon Musk、Marc Andreessen 关注的人?

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people in Silicon Valley have a pretty high bar for who they're willing to follow.
zh: 硅谷很多人对于自己愿意关注谁有相当高的门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of what we do is finding awesome people and connecting them to our companies, otherwise kind of getting them in the A16Z network.
zh: 我们做的很多事情就是找到很棒的人,把他们连接到我们的公司,或者说把他们纳入 A16Z 的网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it allows us to really extend all that network and all that value and all that trust and really that reputation that transfers and builds over time.
zh: 这让我们能真正延伸整个网络、所有那份价值、那份信任,以及那种随时间传递并累积的声誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this Novell quote I love, be so good that people do business through you.
zh: 我很喜欢 Novell 的一句话:要优秀到让人们通过你做生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, if I co-sign two people, they might be able to meet and otherwise build something on a way that I enabled without even having to know about.
zh: 事实上,如果我给两个人背书,他们可能就能相遇并以某种我促成的、甚至无需知晓的方式建立点什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's always hard to match the needs and the skills at exactly the right time.
zh: 但在恰好合适的时机匹配需求与技能总是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we've enabled is this.
zh: 我们所实现的就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the most important opportunities in Silicon Valley start with a simple signal.
zh: 硅谷一些最重要的机会始于一个简单的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone you trust believes in someone you don't know yet.
zh: 你信任的人相信一个你还不认识的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, I sit down with Josh Ellman, Olivia Moore, and David Booth to introduce Cosign, a new product built around professional reputation.
zh: 在这一集里,我与 Josh Ellman、Olivia Moore 和 David Booth 坐下来,介绍 Cosign,一个围绕职业声誉打造的新产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk about why those who believe in you can sometimes say more than a resume, how endorsements can help serve as great people before they're obvious, and why that human signal could become even more valuable as AI makes everything else easier to generate.
zh: 我们谈到为什么相信你的人有时能比一份简历说明更多,背书如何能在人才变得显而易见之前帮助发掘他们,以及为什么当 AI 让其他一切变得更容易生成时,这种人类信号可能变得更有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also get into what we've learned from LinkedIn, X, and AngelList, and what happens when the reputation that normally lives in private conversations and fleeting social posts becomes more visible and durable.
zh: 我们还谈到了我们从 LinkedIn、X 和 AngelList 学到的东西,以及当通常存在于私人对话和转瞬即逝的社交帖子中的声誉变得更可见、更持久时会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're super excited to announce Cosign, a product that is around professional reputation for the startup community and really just trying to be the most comprehensive directory of companies and people.
zh: 我们非常兴奋地宣布 Cosign,一个面向创业社区、围绕职业声誉的产品,真正试图成为最全面的公司与人的名录。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want to start with a story, which is my friend David Perel told me, he said, my Twitter account is more valuable to me than my college education.
zh: 我想从一个故事开始,我的朋友 David Perel 告诉我,他说,我的 Twitter 账号对我来说比我的大学教育更有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, given that I paid a quarter million, whatever it is, my Twitter has given me more value to my career and also personally.
zh: 你知道,考虑到我付了二十五万美元什么的,我的 Twitter 给我的职业生涯以及个人带来了更多价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, we, of course, just launched our own school, so we are big fans of higher education, but I thought that story was profound because, of course, Twitter has been free for so long, and this idea, what he got behind it is, of course, college is a bundle of education, network, and credential.
zh: 当然,我们刚刚创办了自己的学校,所以我们是高等教育的忠实拥趸,但我觉得那个故事很深刻,因为当然,Twitter 已经免费了这么久,而他背后的这个想法是,当然,大学是教育、网络和证书的捆绑包。

speaker: Unknown
en: And social life.
zh: 还有社交生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, of course.
zh: 是的,当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of that is hard to recreate on Twitter, but yeah, exactly.
zh: 其中有些在 Twitter 上很难重现,但是的,完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the education, you learn from having conversations, the network, of course, you meet people, you discover people, kind of is proof of work of if they're interesting, if they're funny, et cetera.
zh: 至于教育,你从对话中学习;至于网络,当然,你结识人、发现人,这某种程度上是他们是否有趣、是否幽默等等的工作证明。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they build something cool, you can discover them.
zh: 如果他们做出了很酷的东西,你就能发现他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the credential thing is really interesting because
zh: 但我觉得证书这件事真的很有意思,因为

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a thought experiment.
zh: 这里有一个思想实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's more impressive to you, someone who went to Stanford or someone who is followed by Patrick Collison, Elon Musk, Marc Andreessen, et cetera?
zh: 对你来说哪个更令人印象深刻,一个上过斯坦福的人,还是一个被 Patrick Collison、Elon Musk、Marc Andreessen 等人关注的人?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think most people would say the latter, right?
zh: 我想大多数人会说后者,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this kind of like peer to peer credential.
zh: 所以这就是这种类似点对点的证书。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what that is,
zh: 而那就是,

speaker: Unknown
en: Implicitly, other people also do this explicitly, is a cosine.
zh: 隐含地——其他人也有明确地这样做——是一种背书(cosign)。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an endorsement that this person is worth tracking.
zh: 这是一种「这个人值得关注」的背书。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a public signal that this person is worth following.
zh: 这是一个「这个人值得追踪」的公开信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think there are lots of other ways to express that signal and create this kind of like reputational benefit that these people get, which is really the exhaust of, this person's not even trying to give them reputational benefit, they're just trying to read what they write.
zh: 而我们认为有很多其他方式可以表达这种信号,并为这些人创造这种声誉上的好处,这其实是——这个人甚至不是想给他们声誉上的好处,他们只是想读他们写的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the exhaust is this endorsement.
zh: 而副产品就是这个背书。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this endorsement, if you're followed by these people, now your doors are open.
zh: 而这个背书,如果你被这些人关注,现在你的大门就打开了。

speaker: Unknown
en: People wanna also read what you say, they wanna work with you, they wanna invest in you, they wanna have you part of their team.
zh: 人们也想读你说的话,想和你共事,想投资你,想让你成为他们团队的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, there's benefit to the receiver, but there's also benefit to the giver too.
zh: 而且不仅接收方有好处,给予方也有好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you're the first person to discover someone,
zh: 因为如果你是第一个发现某个人的人,

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's kind of how Silicon Valley operates.
zh: 嗯,这有点像硅谷的运作方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're gonna be able to hire them quicker.
zh: 你将能更快地雇到他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll be able to fund them quicker.
zh: 你将能更快地投资他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the cool thing about Silicon Valley is you don't know who the next big person is gonna be always.
zh: 而硅谷的酷之处在于,你并不总是知道下一个大人物会是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes they're 18 or come from, you don't come from a name brand school.
zh: 有时他们只有 18 岁,或者来自,你并非来自名校。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're kind of all in this, a little bit of a race to discover talent before anybody else.
zh: 所以我们多少都处在这场比任何人抢先发现人才的竞赛中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, Zach Frankel's done an amazing job, right?
zh: 比如,Zach Frankel 做得非常出色,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So many people have done amazing, of building a reputation for discovering people.
zh: 那么多人做得很出色,建立了善于发现人才的声誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the benefit they get is talent thinks, oh, I can get king made by them.
zh: 所以他们得到的好处是，人才会想，哦，我可以被他们「加冕」（king made）。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if Josh Elliman or Olivia invest in my company, that's a signal to the market.
zh: 比如如果 Josh Elliman 或 Olivia 投资我的公司，那就是给市场的一个信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: And angel investing or just investing from venture firm, that's one way to express a cosign or a signal.
zh: 天使投资或者风险投资机构的投资，是表达这种背书（cosign）或信号的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But a lot of people aren't founders and a lot of people aren't investors.
zh: 但很多人不是创始人，很多人也不是投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we think there are lots of other ways to express this signal.
zh: 所以我们认为还有很多其他方式可以表达这种信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just really curious as you've been building Cosign, like what are the kinds of endorsements you hope to get from the platform?
zh: 我真的很好奇，随着你一直在构建 Cosign，你希望从平台上得到哪些类型的背书？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we want on every profile to have at least three.
zh: 我们希望每个主页上至少有三种。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is who shaped your career?
zh: 第一个是，谁塑造了你的职业生涯？

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we think this sort of like mentor economy, this is what Silicon Valley runs on.
zh: 因为我们认为这种类似导师经济的东西，正是硅谷运转的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: If Josh Elm is my mentor, that means that he is putting, which is true actually.
zh: 如果 Josh Elm 是我的导师，那意味着他在投入——这其实是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just happens to be true.
zh: 这只是碰巧是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was a young person.
zh: 我当时是个年轻人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Josh spent a bunch of time with me.
zh: Josh 花了很多时间在我身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a signal to other people that I'm worth other people spending time with, too, because if you respect Josh, you respect me by association.
zh: 这向其他人传递了一个信号，即我也值得其他人花时间，因为如果你尊重 Josh，你也会因关联而尊重我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's also, again, the benefit to you to discover talent early, to be known.
zh: 而且这对你也有好处，可以尽早发现人才，让自己被人知晓。

speaker: Unknown
en: People want to work with you if you help them.
zh: 如果你帮助过别人，别人就会想和你共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one has shaped my career.
zh: 所以第一个是塑造我职业生涯的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two is would work with anywhere or in the trenches with, because it's hard to tell from existing platforms, like as you were saying the other night, who are you really in the trenches with?
zh: 第二个是「愿意在任何地方共事的人」或「一起在战壕里打拼的人」，因为从现有平台上很难看出，就像你那天晚上说的，你到底和谁真正在战壕里打拼过？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who have you really built bonds with?
zh: 你真正和谁建立了纽带？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who would you go to war with?
zh: 你愿意和谁并肩作战？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who would you, like, no matter what you're doing, you'd want to work with them.
zh: 你会想，无论你在做什么，你都愿意和他们共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a much more granular signal than do I follow them, which could be any number of things.
zh: 这比「我关注了他们」要具体得多，关注可能出于各种原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then third is person to watch.
zh: 然后第三个是值得关注的人（person to watch）。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like who do you think is going to really be emergent, like ascended?
zh: 比如你认为谁会真正崛起，比如迅速上升？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we rank order these two.
zh: 而且我们对这两类进行排序。

speaker: Unknown
en: So platforms just started, most of it's fair game, but in the same way, like to build a great investor profile, it takes many years, but then you've got the credit for doing so.
zh: 所以平台才刚起步，大部分都是可以自由发挥的，但同样的道理，要建立一个出色的投资人主页需要很多年，但之后你会因此获得信誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think you do it around people too.
zh: 我们认为围绕人你也可以这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can say, hey, let's say when you're just starting in your career, I think Olivia is going to be one of the greats.
zh: 所以你可以说，嘿，比如说当你刚进入职业生涯时，我认为 Olivia 会成为最出色的人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think she's a person to watch.
zh: 我觉得她是一个值得关注的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually funny.
zh: 其实挺有意思的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did this experiment seven years ago where I emailed a few hundred people.
zh: 我七年前做过一个实验，我给几百个人发了邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were definitely one of them.
zh: 你肯定是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I asked them for the prison watch.
zh: 我请他们做「值得关注的人」（prison watch，原文如此）的推荐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was just checking today.
zh: 我今天刚查了一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them was Russell Kaplan, who's now the president at Cognition.
zh: 其中一个人是 Russell Kaplan，他现在是 Cognition 的总裁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he was like a 22 year old just engineer at Tesla.
zh: 而他当时还只是 Tesla 一个 22 岁的普通工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's actually signal in that too.
zh: 所以这其实也包含着信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are some of the ones.
zh: 所以这些是其中一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also excited for people to do it for companies too.
zh: 我们也很期待人们为公司也这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what are the companies that you think, right, you know, I'd see, but are going to be great because of course, if you're able to, you can express your conviction with
zh: 比如你认为哪些公司，对，你知道，我会看出来，但会因为什么而变得伟大，因为当然，如果你有能力的话，你可以用钱表达你的信念，

speaker: Unknown
en: You're in money, but not everyone's an investor.
zh: 你在用钱押注，但不是每个人都是投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost like fantasy investing or social capital investing.
zh: 这几乎像是幻想投资（fantasy investing）或者社会资本投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this idea.
zh: 我很喜欢这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like I have long felt this, but as I have invested now for almost a decade, I believe it more and more every week, every day, every month is like the most valuable data in all of Silicon Valley is like who has conviction and who.
zh: 我感觉我很久以来一直有这种感觉，但随着我投资到现在快十年了，我每周、每天、每个月都越来越相信，整个硅谷最有价值的数据就是，谁有信念，以及谁——

speaker: Unknown
en: And who can give you kind of a real read on a person for so many decisions.
zh: 以及谁能让你对一个人有真实的判断，用于那么多决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, who do you invest in?
zh: 比如，你投资谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who do you hire?
zh: 你雇佣谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: What company do you join?
zh: 你会加入哪家公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's such information asymmetry right now.
zh: 而现在信息不对称非常严重。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like our job, investing every day, we are...
zh: 比如我们的工作，每天做投资，我们在……

speaker: Unknown
en: Pinging people saying, hey, do you know anyone who worked with this person?
zh: 不断联系别人，问，嘿，你认识谁和这个人共事过吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we do it every day, and we still, I would say, have to work really hard to find that signal.
zh: 我们每天都这么做，但即便如此，我还是觉得，要找到那种信号必须非常努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how can someone who is maybe evaluating between five startup job offers get that level?
zh: 那么一个可能正在五份创业公司工作邀请之间做评估的人，怎么能获得那种层次的信息？

speaker: Unknown
en: You just can't, especially if you're like an entry-level engineer, and yet that could be the difference between joining like a complete rocket ship and like a company that isn't doing as well.
zh: 你就是做不到，尤其如果你只是一个入门级工程师，而这可能就是加入一艘完整的火箭飞船和一家做得不那么好的公司之间的差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know the data has to be handled carefully around who says what about who, but I think it
zh: 我知道关于谁对谁说了什么的数据必须谨慎处理，但我认为它

speaker: Unknown
en: It will be, and there's like a massive opportunity to add so much value to people's lives and careers.
zh: 它将会，而且这里有一个巨大的机会，可以为人们的生活和职业增添如此多的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk a bit about, because you think a lot about talent discovery.
zh: 聊一聊吧，因为你对人才发现思考了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about the newsletter you did, because I think it's an incredible stuff.
zh: 谈谈你做的那份 newsletter，因为我觉得那是非常了不起的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so my twin sister Justine also works here at Andreessen on our infrastructure team.
zh: 好的，我的双胞胎妹妹 Justine 也在 Andreessen 的基础设施团队工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have both been in venture for basically a decade now.
zh: 我们两个在风投行业基本上都已经干了差不多十年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at our very first venture role, we started a newsletter that we ran every Sunday for I think like six and a half or seven years.
zh: 在我们第一份风投工作里，我们创办了一份 newsletter，我想我们大概每周日运营它，持续了六年半到七年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was basically just aggregating startup job postings.
zh: 它基本上就是聚合创业公司的职位招聘信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thesis was like, we both went to Stanford.
zh: 当时的核心观点是，我们俩都是斯坦福毕业的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We ran a startup incubator at Stanford.
zh: 我们在斯坦福运营过一个创业孵化器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And still, before we were working in a venture firm, we had no way to differentiate between all these startups and founders of who is legitimate, who's not, who's the most exciting.
zh: 即便如此，在我们进入风投公司工作之前，我们也没有办法区分这么多创业公司和创始人，谁是靠谱的，谁不是，谁最令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we were like, OK, we have some inside information now.
zh: 于是我们就想，好，我们现在有一些内部信息了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's curate a list of the companies that we think are worth joining for young people.
zh: 让我们来策划一个清单，列出我们认为值得年轻人加入的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it really, it built up a real community because I think people appreciated it because you can't get that information outside of Silicon Valley.
zh: 它真的建立起了一个真实的社区，因为我觉得大家很感激这件事，因为在硅谷之外你得不到那种信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a network of scouts on campuses that read it and some of those people are now founders that Andreessen has invested in.
zh: 我们在各个校园里有一批读这份 newsletter 的 scout 网络，其中一些人现在成了 Andreessen 投资过的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're off running fantastic companies and in fantastic places.
zh: 他们正在运营着非常棒的公司，处在非常好的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was like the less scalable version of this kind of network.
zh: 所以那算是这种网络的扩展性较低的一个版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm excited for more people to have the ability to kind of put their name behind ideas.
zh: 我很期待有更多人能够把自己的名字背书在观点后面。

speaker: Unknown
